Backups & Upgrades ​

Saidi keeps state in two places: MongoDB, which is the source of truth for every structured record, and a data directory on disk, which holds binary artifacts and a materialized working copy of your memory files. A backup that covers only one of them is not a backup. This page lists exactly what to copy, how versioning works, which migrations the code runs for you, and how to upgrade without losing anything.

What is durable, and where ​

MongoDB — the source of truth ​

src/db/mongo.ts treats MongoDB as required: on disconnect the process terminates rather than accept non-durable changes, and there is deliberately no degraded file-backed mode. The database name is chosen by the mode flag, not by your connection string — src/db/mongo-uri.ts forces the database path to saidi in local mode and saidi_cloud when SAIDI_CLOUD=1, preserving your host, credentials, and query options.

The models under src/db/models/ define what lives there:

Collection areaModel fileHolds
Runsrun.model.tsThe full run record, thread, and usage log
Chatschat.model.tsMain-chat conversations
Crons / Reflexescron.model.ts, reflex.model.tsSchedules and event rules
Playbooksplaybook.model.tsSaved run playbooks
Activityactivity.model.tsThe activity stream
Creditscredit.model.tsWallet + ledger
Memorymemory.model.tsMarkdown memory documents
Agent definitionsagent-def.model.tsPacked custom-agent definitions
Settingssettings.model.tsSystem settings incl. host/port
Secretssecrets.model.tsCredentials, envelope-encrypted under SAIDI_MASTER_KEY
Providers / scan rootsprovider-profiles.model.ts, scan-roots.model.tsModel routing, project scan roots
Channelschannel-config.model.ts, channel-identity.model.tsTelegram and other adapters
Auth / orgsauth.model.ts, org.model.tsUsers, orgs, memberships (cloud)
Migrationsmigration.model.tsCompletion markers for one-time migrations

The data directory — artifacts and working copies ​

resolveDataDir() in src/orchestrator/config.ts picks DATA_DIR in this order: SAIDI_HOME → the repo root when SAIDI_DEV is set → ~/.saidi. In cloud mode every org's state nests one level down under DATA_DIR/orgs/<orgId>/ (src/orchestrator/tenant/paths.ts).

PathContentsReconstructible?
DATA_DIR/config/settings.jsonBind host/port read by the CLI launcher before the server bootsYes — Mongo settings win at runtime
DATA_DIR/config/update-state.jsonAuto-update attempt markerYes
DATA_DIR/memory/global.mdPersonal global memoryMirrored in Mongo
DATA_DIR/memory/members/<userId>/global.mdPer-member personal memory (cloud)Mirrored in Mongo
DATA_DIR/memory/projects/*.mdPer-project memoryMirrored in Mongo
DATA_DIR/memory/agents/*.mdPer-agent memoryMirrored in Mongo
DATA_DIR/memory/learning.jsonLearned preferencesMirrored in Mongo
DATA_DIR/memory/runs/<id>/assets/Run images and deliverables, served as binariesNo
DATA_DIR/memory/runs/<id>/work/<agent>/Per-agent run workspaceNo
DATA_DIR/memory/runs/<id>/repos/<project>/Per-run git worktreesRegenerable from the repo
DATA_DIR/memory/runs/<id>/output/, shared/Sandbox drop zone and handoff notesNo
DATA_DIR/memory/runs/<id>/agent-config/Per-run SDK session state (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)No
DATA_DIR/agents/Custom agent homes: AGENT.md folders, skills, mcp.jsonPacked into Mongo by the migration, but treat as primary
DATA_DIR/orgs/<orgId>/…The same layout, per org (cloud only)—
DATA_DIR/repos/Server-side project clones (cloud)Regenerable from origin

Two rules from the source make this concrete:

  • src/orchestrator/runs/persistence.ts: "Run image assets stay on disk (<runsRoot>/<id>/assets/, served binary); only the JSON run record moves to MongoDB."
  • src/memory/mongo.ts: "Mongo is the source of truth; the on-disk files under the org's memory dir are a materialized working copy." initOrgMemory() deletes disk files that no longer exist in Mongo, so the disk copy is not authoritative for memory.

src/orchestrator/legacy-mongo-migration.ts states the same boundary from the other side: "Binary assets, agent workspaces and provider session files are intentionally not database records and remain on disk."

What to back up ​

Back up both of these, from the same point in time:

  1. The MongoDB database — saidi, or saidi_cloud in cloud mode.
  2. The whole data directory — $SAIDI_HOME, or ~/.saidi if you never set it. In the shipped Docker setup this is the saidi-data volume mounted at /data.

Plus, separately from the automated backup:

  1. MONGODB_URI — it is the one credential that cannot live in Mongo, so it is not inside either backup.
  2. SAIDI_MASTER_KEY, if set. Secrets and provider profiles are envelope-encrypted at rest under it. A database backup without this key is undecryptable.

A minimal procedure:

bash
# 1. Stop the server so debounced writes are drained (SIGTERM triggers the
#    graceful shutdown in src/orchestrator/server.ts).
kill -TERM "$SAIDI_PID"

# 2. Dump the database.
mongodump --uri "$MONGODB_URI" --db saidi --out /backup/mongo-$(date +%F)

# 3. Archive the data directory.
tar -czf /backup/saidi-home-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C "$(dirname "$SAIDI_HOME")" "$(basename "$SAIDI_HOME")"

Stop the server first if you can

gracefulShutdown() in src/orchestrator/server.ts explicitly drains the 400 ms-debounced activity writes and flushes pending run writes before disconnecting Mongo. A snapshot taken while the process is live can miss the last message of a turn, or reload a finishing run as paused.

Run workspaces under memory/runs/<id>/work/ and repos/ can be large. They are the evidence trail for a run — see Runs. If you exclude them to save space, do it deliberately and know that run assets under assets/ are not reconstructible from the database.

How versioning works ​

  • The root package.json version field is the single source of truth. As of this writing it is 1.19.0.
  • src/version.ts imports it directly (import pkg from "../package.json"), so APP_VERSION and the tagged release can never drift.
  • scripts/sync-version.mjs mirrors the root version into client/package.json so the client bundle and the server report the same version. It runs automatically from the npm version lifecycle hook: node scripts/sync-version.mjs && git add client/package.json CHANGELOG.md.
  • CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog, and Saidi follows Semantic Versioning. Releases are generated by release-please from Conventional Commits: fix: → patch, feat: → minor, feat!: or BREAKING CHANGE: → major.
  • RELEASES[0] in src/version.ts carries a fallback release note, stamped by release-please via the x-release-please-version anchor; the in-app "What's New" dialog normally shows the fetched GitHub release body instead.

How updates are detected and installed ​

src/orchestrator/update-check.ts polls the public distribution repo's releases/latest on boot and every 6 hours. Two optional overrides exist: SAIDI_UPDATE_MANIFEST_URL (a JSON manifest, highest priority) and SAIDI_GITHUB_TOKEN (read the private source repo's release instead).

src/orchestrator/auto-update.ts acts on that detection only when all of these hold: settings.autoUpdate is on (default on), local mode, running under the supervisor, running a published dist install, and the target version is not recorded as known-bad in config/update-state.json. When they do, it waits for the orchestrator to go idle and exits with UPDATE_EXIT_CODE (76). The supervisor then runs npm i -g github:saeed9321/saidi-agent between spawns — the install cannot happen in-process because it rewrites the package directory the server is executing from — and relaunches. If the new child dies within 60 seconds, the supervisor reinstalls the previous version. See Deployment & Self-Hosting for the supervisor's exit-code table.

This is why persistent state must live outside the package: npm i -g replaces the package directory on every update.

Migrations the code actually runs ​

All of these are automatic and idempotent unless noted.

1. Legacy in-package state → DATA_DIR ​

migrateLegacyDataDir() in src/orchestrator/data-migrate.ts runs first thing in main(), before anything reads state. Older builds wrote memory/, config/, and agents/ relative to the install directory; this copies them into DATA_DIR — but only when DATA_DIR holds none of those groups yet, so it can never clobber existing data. It is best-effort and never throws.

2. SAIDI_HOME structured records → MongoDB ​

migrateSaidiHomeToMongo() in src/orchestrator/legacy-mongo-migration.ts runs immediately after the Mongo connection succeeds. It imports runs, chats, crons, reflexes, playbooks, the credit wallet and ledger, activity, channel configs and identities, channel sessions, Telegram accounts, memory documents, and packed agent definitions — plus the platform config (settings, secrets, provider profiles, scan roots).

The safety properties are explicit in the source:

  • The completion marker (saidi-home-structured-v1, in the migrations collection) is written only after every discovered record reads back from Mongo, and after the platform config docs are verified to exist.
  • Import operations are idempotent, so a crash before the marker simply retries the incomplete migration on the next boot.
  • Invalid legacy JSON aborts discovery rather than silently setting the marker — there is a test for exactly that (src/orchestrator/legacy-mongo-migration.test.ts).
  • Binary assets, agent workspaces, and provider session files are intentionally left on disk.

3. Memory disk → Mongo, then Mongo → disk ​

initOrgMemory(orgId) in src/memory/mongo.ts runs on org hydration. When Mongo holds no memory docs for the org it performs a one-time disk → Mongo import; thereafter it materializes Mongo docs to files and deletes stale ones. It throws if Mongo is unavailable.

4. Provider selection backfills ​

migrateModelProvider() and migrateRemovedNativeProvider() (src/orchestrator/data-migrate.ts) seed the master model-provider selection for installs that predate it. They run before env hydration, because hydration enforces that selection onto the Anthropic environment variables.

5. Single-user → cloud (manual, one-time) ​

scripts/migrate-to-cloud.mjs is the only migration you invoke yourself. It turns an existing single-user data set into organization #1 of a SAIDI_CLOUD=1 deployment:

  1. Creates the superadmin user (scrypt hash, email pre-verified), the organization, and the owner membership.
  2. Backfills orgId (and createdBy where a human owns the record) onto runs, crons, reflexes, activityevents, and creditledgers.
  3. Re-keys the credit wallet document from default to the new orgId.
  4. Moves DATA_DIR/memory and DATA_DIR/agents to DATA_DIR/orgs/<orgId>/.
bash
SAIDI_MIGRATE_PASSWORD='at-least-10-chars' \
node scripts/migrate-to-cloud.mjs \
  --email you@example.com \
  --name "Said" \
  --org-name "Acme" \
  --seats 5 \
  --dry-run

The password comes from the environment so it never lands in shell history, and must be 10+ characters unless --dry-run is passed. The script always targets the saidi_cloud database regardless of the SAIDI_CLOUD flag in your shell. It is idempotent — an already-migrated deployment is detected and each step is skipped. Run it with --dry-run first, then without. Its own header says it plainly: back up the data directory and Mongo before running, because step 4 moves directories.

When it finishes, start the server with SAIDI_CLOUD=1 and log in. Note that cloud mode requires SAIDI_MASTER_KEY for tenant secret encryption.

Safe upgrade procedure ​

  1. Read the changelog. Check CHANGELOG.md for the versions between yours and the target, and look for BREAKING CHANGE entries. Your running version is in the UI and in the root package.json.

  2. Take a backup. Both the database and $SAIDI_HOME, per the procedure above. Do not skip this even for a patch bump — migrations run automatically at boot and some of them move files.

  3. Stop the server with SIGTERM so the graceful shutdown drains debounced writes.

  4. Upgrade the code.

    From a source checkout:

    bash
    git pull
npm run setup
npm run build

    From a published install:

    bash
    npm i -g github:saeed9321/saidi-agent

    In Docker with docker-compose.dist.yml: bump the SAIDI_REF build arg to the new tag and run docker compose up -d --build. Do not use the in-app update dialog inside a container — it would install over the image layer and the change would vanish on the next recreate.

  5. Confirm SAIDI_HOME still points at the same directory. This is the most common way to "lose" data on upgrade: the resolution order is SAIDI_HOME → repo root (only with SAIDI_DEV) → ~/.saidi, and a changed environment silently starts you on an empty install.

  6. Start the server and watch the boot log. A first boot after an upgrade may print Migrated existing Saidi data (…) → <DATA_DIR> or Migrated SAIDI_HOME structured state to MongoDB (N runs, N chats, N activity rows). Both are expected once.

  7. Verify. Check that runs, memory, and agents are present in the UI, and that /api/health answers. From a source checkout you can also run npm run typecheck and npm test.

  8. If the new version misbehaves, stop it, reinstall the previous version, and restore the backup. Under the supervisor a post-update crash inside 60 seconds triggers an automatic rollback to the prior version; outside that window you roll back by hand.

Rolling back ​

There is no down-migration. The forward migrations are additive to Mongo (import and backfill) with one exception: scripts/migrate-to-cloud.mjs moves memory/ and agents/ under orgs/<orgId>/. Rolling back across that point means restoring your pre-migration data directory and database from backup, not un-running the script.
